title: Alphabet's Isomorphic Labs seeks valuation of at least $40 billion in new funding round
source_used: Bloomberg report as relayed by Yahoo Finance Canada
key_facts: Isomorphic Labs, an AI drug-discovery startup spun out of Google DeepMind, is in early talks to raise funding at a valuation of at least $40 billion.
It could be valued as high as $50 billion; talks are ongoing and terms could change, per a Bloomberg report.
Five months ago it raised $2.1 billion in a Series B round with substantial backing from Alphabet.
Founded in 2021 to build on AlphaFold, DeepMind's system for predicting protein structures; partners include Eli Lilly and Novartis.
None of the AI drug discovery companies has brought an AI-designed medicine to market.
Demis Hassabis remains chief executive of Isomorphic Labs after moving to a DeepMind chairman role in August.
quote_evidence: Isomorphic Labs, the artificial intelligence (AI) drug discovery startup spun out of Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOG)'s Google DeepMind, is in early talks to raise new funding at a valuation of at least $40 billion.
The London-based company could be valued as high as $50 billion in the financing, although the talks are ongoing and terms could change before any deal closes, a report by Bloomberg said.

The potential valuation would represent a sharp increase from just five months ago, when Isomorphic Labs raised $2.1 billion in a Series B funding round that included substantial backing from Alphabet.
why_it_matters_hint: Investors are reportedly ready to value an AI drug-discovery company at $40 billion or more before it has an approved medicine.
notes: Bloomberg original not read (paywall); text from Yahoo Finance Canada rewrite of the Bloomberg report. Early talks only.
